page.title: AI Content Creation: Turn Ideas Into Carousels & Posts

findings.title: Page scrolls sideways on a phone (405px wide at 390px)
findings.evidence: e.g. span.whitespace-nowrap “Start Creating Visuals That” ends at 405px.
findings.fix: Find the fixed-width element (tables, code blocks, images, grids with min-width) and give it max-width: 100% or overflow-x: auto. Test at 390px.

findings.title: 5 different corner radii on panels
findings.evidence: Radii in use on ≥80px panels: 14px, 18px, 20px, 22px, 24px. A system usually needs two or three.
findings.fix: Define --radius-sm / --radius-md / --radius-lg tokens and use only those.

findings.title: Gradient-filled text (3)
findings.evidence: div.text-[140px].leading-[0.85] “1” uses background-clip: text with a gradient. Decorative, hurts contrast, and reads as generated.
findings.fix: Use a solid colour. Emphasis comes from size and weight, not a rainbow.

findings.title: Rounded icon tile above 6 headings
findings.evidence: 6 near-square 40px boxes with a background sit directly above headings. The icon-in-a-tinted-square above every feature title is the default generated feature grid.
findings.fix: Remove the tile backgrounds and let the icon sit inline with the heading, or drop the icons and let the headings carry the row.

findings.title: Aphoristic-cadence copy
findings.evidence: “5 aphoristic constructions: "No Design Skills Needed. No prompts."”
findings.fix: Three or more sections landing on a short rebuttal sentence ("X. No Y." / "X. Just Y.") or a manufactured-contrast aphorism ("Not a feature. A platform.") reads as AI cadence, not voice. Once is fine; the pattern is the tell.

findings.title: A lone badge “200+ Happy Creators” that does nothing
findings.evidence: A 238×36px pill that is not clickable, is not one of a set of tags, and labels something the surrounding text already makes clear. Badges imply a category system; a single one is decoration.
findings.fix: Delete it. If the information matters, fold it into the sentence next to it. Reserve pills for things that are actually one of several (filters, statuses, tags you can click).
findings.citation: no-slop ‘status pill with dot’ heuristic (MIT); Fountain Institute tell #7 (status dots)

findings.title: One h2 is a different size from the other 7
findings.evidence: “Got questions? We've got answers.” is 52px; the other h2s are 56/60px (52px ×1, 56px ×5, 60px ×2). Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h2 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: 36 rounded panels on one page
findings.evidence: Rounded corners on every container is one of the ranked vibe-coded tells (#5 in the Reddit corpus).
findings.fix: Round the things that are interactive or elevated; let sections and layout containers stay square.

findings.title: Inter for 100% of the text
findings.evidence: Primary family is Inter, one of the fonts generated UIs default to. Fonts seen: Inter.
findings.fix: Not wrong on its own. If everything else is default too, this is the cheapest thing to change: pick one typeface with a point of view for headings and keep the workhorse for body.
findings.citation: Impeccable overused-font; HN thread on vibe-coded tells (Inter everywhere)

findings.title: Eyebrow chip above the hero headline
findings.evidence: “200+ Happy Creators” (13px, pill) sits directly above a 72px h1. The tiny label + giant headline pairing is the default generated SaaS hero.
findings.fix: Fold the label into the headline or the first sentence. If it's an announcement, make it a real link somewhere else.

findings.title: Centered hero: big headline, centered sub, centered buttons
findings.evidence: h1 at 72px, centered, with 4 centered blocks under it. On 23.5% of Show HN launches. It's the layout every builder emits when nobody chooses one.
findings.fix: Not a problem on its own, but combined with other tells it's the skeleton. Left-align and put the product next to the headline, or lead with the product itself.

findings.title: Blurred colour blobs behind the content (1)
findings.evidence: section.py-[80px].sm:py-[180px] is a radial-gradient wash. The aurora backdrop is the default "atmosphere" of generated heroes.
findings.fix: Remove it and let the content carry the first screen. If you want atmosphere, use one real image.

findings.title: 1 marketing buzzword
findings.evidence: “…ting Visuals That Drive Results Today Try Creato…”
findings.fix: Replace each with the specific thing: what it does, for whom, with a number if you have one. 'Streamline your workflow' → 'Turns a 40-minute export into a button.'

hits: ting Visuals That Drive Results Today Try Creato

findings.title: h3 is used at 3 sizes, consistently
findings.evidence: Sizes: 18px ×6, 20px ×5, 34px ×4. “Turn Idea Into Carousel That People Save” is 34px, “Your Brand. Every Time.” is 18px. Each size is used more than once, so this is a system rather than drift; but it means the same tag is doing two jobs.
findings.fix: If the 18px ones are sub-sections, make them h4. Screen readers and search engines only see the tag.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: 16 status dots on the page
findings.evidence: Coloured dots attached to labels where a word would say more.
findings.fix: Replace with text or remove.

findings.title: 2 cards nested inside other cards
findings.evidence: 2 outer containers with bordered/shadowed children, e.g. div.rounded-b-[14px].bg-[#F6F6F6] inside div.rounded-[22px].bg-white. Every layer of box is a layer the reader has to look through.
findings.fix: Remove the inner border/background and separate items with spacing or a divider. One container per idea.
findings.citation: UXly nested-panel (MIT); Fountain Institute tell #5; Reinecke 2013: visual complexity is the strongest negative predictor of appeal

findings.title: Stat banner: 1 · 2 · 3
findings.evidence: A row of 3 big numbers with small labels. On 12% of Show HN launches. Real numbers are fine; the pattern reads as template when the numbers are round, unsourced, or "99.9% uptime" on a weekend project.
findings.fix: Keep it only if each number is real, specific and checkable (link the source). Otherwise fold the one true number into a sentence.
